Then `add_operation { "kind": "Wire Contour", "source": "<model>", "params": { "condition": "<condition id>", "side": "die"|"punch", "start": [x, y] } }` with no `tool` (fields: `top_z`, `bottom_z`, `condition`, `side`, `start`). `edit_operation` patches `side`, `start` and `condition`. Refusals arrive as tool errors in the command's words: a tool named, no or unknown condition, a condition with no gap or wire diameter; the start hole and the corner minimum are refused at `generate`. Give `undersize` (mm per side, 0 or more) or `condition` (a machine EDM condition id, read from the setup's sinker EDM; `setup` names that setup, default the active one), not both; `stub` (more than 0) is how far the electrode stands above the cavity's mouth; `pickup` (0 or more) is the offset from the electrode's top to the measuring reference. `orbit` makes it that much smaller again per side. +- **Through-hole break-through (#1557, #2441)**: `add_operation` and `edit_operation` take `"break_through"` in `params` for Drill, Bore and Thread: how far past a through hole's floor the cut runs, in mm. `null` is the default and means the kind's own 1.0 mm; the reply leaves the key out until it is stated. A negative or non-finite value is refused on creation and edit. Drill also takes `"break_through_from"`, the Holes page's "Break-through from": `"full_diameter"` ("Full diameter", the default) adds the drill point length, so the full diameter clears the hole; `"tip"` ("Tip", the behaviour of project files before v68) stops the drill tip at the floor minus `break_through`. Any other value is refused. Example: `edit_operation { "name": "Drill1", "params": { "break_through": 0.5, "break_through_from": "tip" } }`. `list_operation_types` lists `break_through` (`number`, default `null`) for drill, bore and thread, and `break_through_from` (`string`, default `"full_diameter"`) for drill. A spot cycle stops above the through floor, so no break-through applies. At `generate` the path's notes say how far the holes run past the part bottom; an exit into a modelled fixture under the stock is a fixture hit that holds the post. A lathe's axial and cross holes refuse a stated break-through by name.

Turns about the part's bounds centre, composed onto the setup's current part alignment; the work offset is untouched; one undo step. Refused by name: a face, a curved edge as the one pick, an edge in a point pair that is not circular (straight, or no circle within tolerance), coincident points, a single pick along Z, X and Y picks running (nearly) along each other.

+
+

+        root = skill_dir.parents[2]
+        skill = (skill_dir / "SKILL.md").read_text()

+            with self.subTest(text=text):
+                self.assertIn(text, row)
+        # The wire values are the file DTO's snake_case names, default first.
+        params = (root / "crates/app/src/project/params.rs").read_text()
+        dto = re.search(r"pub enum BreakThroughFromDto \{(.*?)\}", params, re.S)

+            with self.subTest(value=value):
+                self.assertIn(f'"{value}"', row)

+## #2840 - pin golden, machine, STEP and workflow fixtures to LF in .gitattributes
+
+- **Chosen:** pin all test fixtures, golden post outputs, machine definitions, STEP/STP models, agent and skill definitions, and GitHub workflows to LF line endings (`text eol=lf`) in `.gitattributes`.
+  - Why: Git for Windows checks out text files with CRLF by default (`core.autocrlf=true`). Test suites comparing post programs byte-for-byte (such as `explain_fanuc_family`), parsing machine definitions (such as `wire-iso-fixture.mch`), importing STEP models (`import_step_curve_guard`), and xtask tests parsing skill markdown or workflow concurrency blocks expect and require LF line endings (`\n`).
+  - Dropped: modifying individual tests to accept CRLF. Normalizing line endings at the repository boundary via `.gitattributes` guarantees deterministic behavior across platforms without weakening byte-exact golden test assertions.
+- **Pinning tests:**
+  - `xtask/tests/example_line_endings.rs`: added `all_golden_and_fixture_files_have_eol_lf` asserting that `git check-attr eol` reports `lf` across all golden, recorded, machine, STEP, skill, and workflow directories.
+  - `xtask/tests/example_line_endings.rs`: added `golden_and_fixture_files_keep_lf_with_autocrlf` asserting that checked-out files maintain LF line endings without carriage returns under `core.autocrlf=true`.
+  - Verified affected suites pass cleanly: `explain_fanuc_family`, `wire_taper_angle`, `import_step_curve_guard`, and `post_merge_concurrency`.
